analysis_steps.goal: Model ionized gas [C II] 158-um emission using photoionization modelling

method.value: Run MAPPINGS V photoionization models with STARBURST99 ionizing spectra in a 1D plane-parallel geometry to predict [C II] 158 um, C II] 2325 A, and C III] 1909 A line ratios as a function of starburst age, ionization parameter U, and electron density n_e, and combine with observed Keck UV line fluxes to estimate ionized gas [C II] 158 um luminosity.

evidence.quote: We address this question by using photoionization modelling to predict the [C II ] 158- _µ_ m emission from the ionized ISM using the M APPINGS V photoionization code (Allen et al. 2008; Groves & Allen 2010).

To set the ionizing radiation field, we use the S TARBURST 99 stellar population models [4] (Leitherer et al. 1999, 2010), including also the effects of stellar rotation on the emitted spectra of massive stars, as described in Levesque et al. (2012).
We adopt a one-dimensional plane-parallel geometry as appropriate for the expected geometry in SL2S 0217: a screen of ionized ISM on front of an ionizing cluster.

key_parameters.value: Z = 0.05 Z_sun, n_e = 10 and 100 cm^-3, starburst age step = 0.5 Myr (0.5-5.0 Myr), log U = -4.0 to -1.5

evidence.quote: Following the B18 modelling of the UV spectrum, we set the model metallicity to 0 _._ 05 _Z_ _⊙_ and assume an instantaneous starburst.

We explore models with electron densities between _n_ _e_ =10 and 100 cm _[−]_ [3], since the C II ] 2325 A/ [˚] [C II ] 158 _µ_ m flux ratio is very sensitive to density due to the low critical density of the [CII] 158 _µ_ m line in ionised gas ( _n_ _e_ =50 cm [3] ).
We vary the ionization parameter _U_ (defined as the ratio of the _≥_ 13 _._ 6 eV photon number density and the gas density _n_ ) and the age of the ionizing star cluster (in steps of 0.5 Myr).

assumptions.value: Uniform ISM, 1D plane-parallel geometry, instantaneous starburst with stellar rotation, no PDR contribution.

evidence.quote: The photoionization modelling provides a lower limit on _L_ [CII], as the contribution of [C II ] 158 _µ_ m from photon-dominated regions (PDRs) (e.g., Hollenbach & Tielens 1997) is not included in the M APPINGS models.
Here, we treat the ISM as uniform.

validation.value: Compared predicted line intensities across different stellar model libraries (differing by <= 0.1 dex).

evidence.quote: For the case considered here, the predicted line intensities differ only marginally ( _≤_ 0 _._ 1 dex) between the different stellar model libraries.

claims.hypothesis: Locally-calibrated [C II]-SFR relations for dwarf galaxies (e.g., De Looze et al. 2014) and metallicity-dependent high-z simulation models accurately predict [C II] luminosity in high-redshift metal-poor dwarf galaxies.
claims.experiment: Measure the source-plane [C II] 158-um luminosity upper limit in SL2S 0217 (Z = 0.05 Z_sun, SFR = 23 M_sun/yr) using deep ALMA Band 9 imaging and visibility-plane analysis and compare against empirical and simulation-based [C II]-SFR relations.
claims.result: The source-plane [C II]/SFR ratio is <= 1 x 10^6 L_sun/(M_sun yr^-1), which matches the metallicity-dependent simulation predictions of Vallini et al. (2015) and Olsen et al. (2017) but is at least 30x fainter (>= 4 sigma tension) than predicted by the De Looze et al. (2014) relation.
claims.finding: Extrapolating locally-calibrated [C II]-SFR relations to high-redshift, metal-poor galaxies is dangerous, whereas metallicity-dependent hydrodynamical simulations accurately reproduce the faint [C II] emission.

evidence.quote: However, the [C II ] line is 30 _×_ fainter than predicted by the De Looze et al. [C II ]-SFR relation for local dwarfs, illustrating the danger of extrapolating locally-calibrated relations to high-redshift, metal-poor galaxies.

evidence.loc: 4.2. Comparison with empirical models and simulations
evidence.quote: Our upper limit is in agreement with the metallicitydependent relations of Vallini et al. (2015) and Olsen et al. (2017).

evidence.loc: 4.2. Comparison with empirical models and simulations
evidence.quote: On the other hand, the [C II ] emission in SL2S 0217 is at least 30 _×_ fainter than expected from the locallycalibrated De Looze et al. (2014), a _≥_ 4 _σ_ tension.

claims.hypothesis: The ionized ISM can account for the entire [C II] 158-um emission in the low-metallicity, strongly-ionizing galaxy SL2S 0217.
claims.experiment: Use MAPPINGS V photoionization models coupled with STARBURST99 spectra and observed Keck UV C II] 2325 A and C III] 1909 A fluxes to predict the [C II] 158-um luminosity from the ionized gas.
claims.result: For n_e = 100 cm^-3, the predicted on-sky ionized [C II] luminosity is ~7.3 x 10^7 L_sun, about 5x below the observed upper limit (<= 3.4 x 10^8 L_sun), allowing up to 80% of [C II] to originate from neutral/molecular gas (PDRs), though for n_e = 10 cm^-3 and log U >= -3.5 the predicted ionized [C II] exceeds the upper limit.
claims.finding: Up to 80% of the [C II] emission can originate from neutral or molecular gas, although a fully ionized ISM cannot be ruled out at low electron densities.

evidence.quote: Photoionization modelling indicates that up to 80% of the [C II ] emission originates from neutral or molecular gas, although we can not rule out that the gas is fully ionized.

For most of the _n_ _e_, _U_ models considered here, our [C II ] 158 _µ_ m upper limit is higher than the contribution from the ionized ISM; the neutral/molecular ISM can account for up to 80% of the [C II ] 158 _µ_ m line flux, similar to the _z_ = 0 low-metallicity galaxies (Croxall et al. 2017; Cormier et al. 2019).
However, in the low-density, high-ionization regime ( _n_ _e_ = 10 cm _[−]_ [3], log _U_ _≥−_ 3 _._ 5), the predicted [C II ] 158- _µ_ m luminosity exceeds our upper limits.

why_this_data.value: SL2S 0217 is strongly lensed (magnification ~17) at z = 1.844 with a low metallicity (0.05 Z_sun) and stellar mass ~10^8 M_sun, providing an accessible analogue of Epoch of Reionization galaxies; [C II] 158-um in ALMA Band 9 is the brightest probe of cool gas in metal-poor galaxies.

evidence.quote: Our best bet for probing the molecular gas content of this metal-poor galaxies is the [C II ] 158- _µ_ m line, thanks to its low critical density and large intrinsic brightness.

Thanks to its large magnification, SL2S 0217 provides a unique opportunity to detect the neutral ISM in a high-redshift EELG with a stellar mass of just 10 [8] _M_ _⊙_ - 1 dex lower than any previous _z_ _∼_ 2 study.

why_this_method.value: Baselines > 1000 klambda were discarded and uv-tapering (1.0 arcsec) with a large (R <= 3 kpc) aperture was used to maximize surface-brightness sensitivity and account for potentially extended or spatially offset [C II] emission; (u,v)-plane fitting was performed to check for spatial filtering effects; C II] 2325 A was used in photoionization modelling to avoid systematic uncertainties from carbon abundance and ionization state.

evidence.quote: For the C43-6 configuration, we discard all baselines longer than 1000 k _λ_, as adding the long baselines significantly reduces the surface brightness sensitivity of the combined dataset.

evidence.loc: 3.1.2. Searching for signal in the (u,v) plane
evidence.quote: The 1.0-arcsec taper maximizes the surface-brightness sensitivity, while large aperture size accounts for a potentially very extended [C II ] emission.
Using C II ] instead of any of the other UV lines detected in the Keck spectrum by B18 avoids systematic uncertainties related to the carbon abundance and ionization state.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Modelling the neutral/molecular PDR phase directly was refrained from due to the lack of observational constraints (only [C II] 158-um and weak CO(2-1) upper limits).

evidence.quote: Due to the lack of constraints on the PDR phase (just our [C II ] 158- _µ_ m and a very weak CO(2–1) upper limits, we refrain from modelling the neutral/molecular ISM.

limitations_admitted.value: Extracting flux measurements from dirty images over extended apertures can be biased because the area under a dirty beam integrates to zero for large apertures (though sidelobes are <= 5% here).

evidence.loc: 3.1.1. Searching for signal in the image plane
evidence.quote: Consequently, flux measurements extracted from _dirty_ images over extended areas might be biased, particularly in presence of strong positive or negative sidelobes.

limitations_admitted.value: Photoionization modelling treats the ISM as uniform, whereas the UV spectral slope varies across the source and the C II], [C II], and C III] lines are likely not co-spatial on sub-kiloparsec scales.

evidence.quote: Here, we treat the ISM as uniform. However, as shown by E19, the UV spectral slope varies considerably across the source; the C II ], [C II ] and C III ] lines are thus likely not co-spatial on sub-kiloparsec scales.

limitations_admitted.value: Lack of electron density constraints implies a ~1 dex uncertainty in the MAPPINGS-predicted [C II] 158-um / C II] 2325 A flux ratio.

reproducibility.score_reason: The paper clearly states the ALMA project codes, antenna flags, reference antenna, uv-cutoff (1000 klambda), weighting, uv-tapers, spectral binning, and MAPPINGS V input parameters. However, reproducing the exact aperture photometry requires the external lens model from Cooray et al. (2011) and manual re-calibration of the Band 9 visibilities without full calibration script details.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Both ALMA datasets (2016.1.00142.S and 2016.1.00776.S) are public in the ALMA archive, the flagging and imaging recipe (discarding >1000 klambda baselines, natural weighting, 0.5 and 1.0 arcsec tapers) is specific, and the main results are quantitative rms sensitivities and flux/luminosity upper limits.
